title: Start free with OpenRouter in {name}: one account, then answers
description: The quickest way to get answers in {name}: a free OpenRouter account, made on its site in a minute. What it gives, its daily limits, and what can cost money.
answer: Send your first request, and press {free}. OpenRouter’s site opens: make a free account there, allow {name} to use it, and you come back to your request, answered.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {brains}. With no brain yet, the first request you send shows {first}, whose {free} is this same way.
need: An email address, or an account OpenRouter lets you sign in with, to make its account.
Nothing to pay: its free brains need no payment method.
steps: Write a request in the box and send it. With no brain yet, {name} shows {first}: press {free}.
Or, at any time: open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {brains}, press {add}, choose {quick}, and press {action}.
OpenRouter’s site opens in the same tab. Make an account there, or sign in to the one you have.
OpenRouter asks whether {name} may use your account: allow it.
You come back to {name}, which says {connected} and answers the request you sent.
good: {name} has no tie to OpenRouter, nor to any other service it offers.
OpenRouter gives access to hundreds of brains. Some are free, within daily limits; the others are paid for with credits you add on its site.
{name} asks OpenRouter to send your requests only to services that neither keep nor train on them.
OpenRouter’s answers come from the cloud. For what should stay on this computer, add a brain on this device too: see {device}.
The key OpenRouter gives {name} stays on this device, encrypted, and is never in a backup.
OpenRouter’s terms are for adults, so a child’s profile doesn’t offer it.
fixes: You came back, and no brain is connected
The sign-in didn’t finish. Press {free} again, or {action} in {brains}, and allow {name} on OpenRouter’s site.
{name} says the brain is out of credits
The version answering isn’t free, and the account has no credits for it. Add credits on OpenRouter’s site, or choose a free one on its page in {settings} › {brains}, under {version}.
Its free brains’ daily limit is reached. Wait until tomorrow, add credits on OpenRouter’s site, or add a brain of another kind: see {choose}.
ask: Which brain answers me now, and is it free?
